title: Total quotient rings commute with etale base change over reduced Noetherian rings
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is reduced, meaning that $a^n=0$ with $n\geq1$ implies $a=0$. Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a commutative ring $R$ let $T_R$ be its multiplicative set of non-zero-divisors, namely the elements $t$ for which $tr=0$ implies $r=0$ for every $r$, and put $Q(R)=T_R^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $f(T_A)\subseteq T_B$, and the canonical $B$-algebra map
$$Q(A)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow Q(B),\qquad (a/s)\otimes b\longmapsto f(a)b/f(s)$$
is an isomorphism. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The zero rings and the map $A\to0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0EN6 (lemma-meromorphic-quasi-coherent), proof of (1)-(2), displayed map Q(A) tensor_A B to Q(B), specialized to reduced Noetherian A. The proof uses Algebra Tag 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points) and Tag 05C3 (lemma-weakly-ass-zero-divisors).

proof.text: Put $S=T_A$ and $T=T_B$. The étale morphism is flat by its definition; the affine flatness criterion makes $B$ a flat $A$-module. For $s\in S$, tensor the injective $A$-linear multiplication map $A\xrightarrow{s}A$ with $B$. The definition of flatness says the resulting multiplication map $B\xrightarrow{f(s)}B$ is injective (the identifications $A\otimes_AB=B$ send $a\otimes b$ to $f(a)b$). Thus $f(S)\subseteq T$, including when $B=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EN6, lemma-meromorphic-quasi-coherent, proof: parenthesis defining the displayed arrow by flatness.

proof.text: Let $C=Q(A)\otimes_AB$. Localization base change, with the tensor factors interchanged by $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$, identifies $C$ as the $B$-algebra $f(S)^{-1}B$. Write $j:B\to C$ for $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Every element is $j(b)j(f(s))^{-1}$ for some $s\in S$. The localization zero criterion says $j(b)=0$ precisely when $f(s)b=0$ for some $s\in S$; Step 1 then gives $b=0$. In particular $j$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00CM, section-localization; base change of localization as in the displayed map in spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0EN6.

proof.text: Apply the reduced Noetherian total-fraction decomposition to $A$. It supplies finitely many fields $K_i=A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and the compatible $A$-algebra isomorphism $Q(A)\cong\prod_iK_i$. Tensoring this isomorphism with $B$ and applying the finite-product tensor isomorphism gives $C\cong\prod_i C_i$, where $C_i=K_i\otimes_AB$. Although the finite-product result is stated for modules, its map is also a ring map here: on pure tensors the formula $(x_i)_i\otimes b\mapsto(x_i\otimes b)_i$ preserves the unit and multiplication; bilinearity extends that equality to sums of pure tensors. Therefore this is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 0EN6, lemma-meromorphic-quasi-coherent, proof: Q(A) as product of minimal-prime localizations; Algebra Tags 02LX and 00EU in the reduced case.

proof.text: The affine fibre-product identification gives $\operatorname{Spec}C_i=\operatorname{Spec}K_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}B$, with its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ the base change of the given étale morphism. Étale base change makes this morphism étale. The field-algebra structure theorem now gives $C_i\cong\prod_{h=1}^{n_i}L_{ih}$, with each $L_{ih}$ a finite separable extension field of $K_i$ and $n_i\geq0$. Combining these isomorphisms with Step 3 expresses $C$ as a finite product of fields, allowing the empty product.

source.place: Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field; Morphisms Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; Schemes Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes. This specializes the local-ring factors of Tag 0EN6 to fields.

proof.text: For $t\in T$ multiplication by $j(t)$ on $C$ is injective: if $j(t)j(b)j(f(s))^{-1}=0$, the fraction zero criterion gives $f(u)tb=0$ for some $u\in S$; since both $f(u)$ and $t$ are non-zero-divisors in $B$, this implies $b=0$. In a finite product of fields an element with injective multiplication has no zero coordinate: a zero coordinate would annihilate the nonzero vector which is $1$ there and $0$ elsewhere. Taking the inverse in each coordinate thus makes $j(t)$ a unit in $C$. In the empty product, $C=0$ and its unique element is a unit as well.

source.place: Tag 00CM, section-localization, fraction equivalence and zero criterion; elementary coordinate calculation after Tag 00U3.

proof.text: Define $\alpha:C\to Q(B)$ on localization fractions by $j(b)j(f(s))^{-1}\mapsto b/f(s)$; Step 1 and the fraction relation make it well-defined. Define $\beta:Q(B)\to C$ by $b/t\mapsto j(b)j(t)^{-1}$ using Step 5. If $v(t^{\prime}b-tb^{\prime})=0$ with $v\in T$, then $j(v)$, $j(t)$ and $j(t^{\prime})$ are units, proving equality of the two images; addition and multiplication follow directly from the fraction formulas. These are $B$-algebra maps. Their composites fix respectively every fraction $b/t$ and every fraction $j(b)j(f(s))^{-1}$, so they are inverse. Finally $(a/s)\otimes b=j(f(a)b)j(f(s))^{-1}$, whence $\alpha((a/s)\otimes b)=f(a)b/f(s)$, the required canonical map. If $A=0$ a unital map forces $B=0$; all constructions above still hold, as they also do for arbitrary $A\to0$.
